events.title: Umayyad conquest of Sindh
hints: A teenaged commander led an army along the Makran coast in the early eighth century.
The ruler Dahir was defeated and killed at a battle near Rohri in 712.
The Indus delta became a distant province of a caliphate based in Damascus.
events.summary: Led by Muhammad bin Qasim, an Umayyad army conquered the lower Indus region in 711 to 713, defeating Raja Dahir. Sindh became a province of the Caliphate, which collected taxes from it and gained a foothold on Indian Ocean trade routes.

events.title: East India Company conquest of Sindh
hints: A general overthrew the ruling Talpur emirs after a pair of battles.
The decisive fight in February 1843 was at Miani.
A famous one-word Latin pun about the conquest was invented by a humour magazine.
events.summary: Under Sir Charles Napier, East India Company forces defeated the Talpur Mirs at Miani and Dubba in 1843 and annexed Sindh. The campaign followed a revised treaty the Mirs had signed under pressure, and gave the Company control of the lower Indus.
events.quip: The famous 'Peccavi' dispatch ('I have Sind') was a magazine joke. The annexation, regrettably, was not.

events.title: Annexation of the Punjab and the Koh-i-Noor
hints: A one-eyed maharaja's empire outlived him by only a decade.
Two wars with a trading company ended with a boy ruler being deposed in 1849.
A famous diamond was surrendered to a distant queen as part of the settlement.
events.summary: After two Anglo-Sikh wars, the East India Company annexed the Sikh Empire in 1849. Under the Treaty of Lahore, the Koh-i-Noor diamond was surrendered to Queen Victoria and the young Maharaja Duleep Singh was deposed.

events.title: The Durand Line and the North-West Frontier
hints: A frontier line was drawn through mountain communities with no vote from them.
The resulting border province was ruled under special regulations aimed at tribal areas.
events.summary: The 1893 Durand Line placed the Pashtun tribal belt on the British side of a new frontier. It was governed as a distinct frontier province from 1901, with special regulations such as the Frontier Crimes Regulation, a buffer in the Great Game with Russia.
